title: Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage: Applying Payments and Returned Payments
content:
**Rule.** Every payment is applied to one named coinsurance charge and only up to that charge's open balance; a payment meant for several charges is split one row per charge, oldest service month first, and any remainder beyond the open charges is not posted but returned to the payer. A resident or representative pays by one of the accepted resident payment methods; a single card payment may not exceed the card payment maximum, and an amount above it must be split across another accepted method. Carrier and state remittances post as a Medigap remittance or a Medicaid crossover remittance against the secondary charge. A dishonored payment is reversed against the payment entry it came from for the full amount that entry applied, which reinstates the charge. A payment entry is reversed at most once. Once the resident has had the returned-payment limit of dishonored payments within the rolling lookback of calendar months ending on the payment date, only certified funds are accepted from the resident on any coverage episode. Statements for the prior service month issue on the statement day of the month to tiers that issue resident statements, and the resident amount is due within the payment due days after the statement date; Part A coinsurance carries no late charge.

These are the Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage cashiering standards. The accepted methods, the card maximum, the returned-payment limit and lookback, the certified-funds methods, the statement day and the due days are the figures of the statements and payment terms schedule; whether a tier issues resident statements is that tier's own entry there.

**Open balance of a charge** — its amount less the payments and adjustments posted against it, plus any returned payments.

**Returned-payment count** — the dishonored payments reversed for the resident within the rolling lookback of calendar months ending on the payment date, across all of the resident's coverage episodes.

| Returned payments in the lookback | Methods accepted from the resident |
|---|---|
| Fewer than the limit | Any accepted resident payment method |
| At the limit or more | Certified funds only |

*Hypothetical worked example:* a payer sends 815.00 toward two resident charges with open balances of 340.00 (earlier service month) and 410.00 (later). 340.00 is applied to the earlier charge, 410.00 to the later one, and the remaining 65.00 is not posted but returned.
